title: Al-Basit, the Expander
hookLine: the Expander, who opens and widens
tomorrow: a reporter wants one photo of 'the artist.' who stands in it?

cards: The first full breath after a long cry is different from every other breath. The ribs widen, the shoulders drop, and there's room again. Yesterday asked: does it ever open back up?
The same verse that names the tightening answers in its next word: "Allah straiteneth and enlargeth." Today is the enlarging.

teach.b: Al-Basit, the Expander, who opens and widens.

teach.h: THE SAME HAND CLOSES AND OPENS.
teach.b: In the traditional list of names it stands right beside al-Qabid, and they make most sense as a pair: the hand that closes is the same hand that opens. The Qur'an gives the widening a body.
A short surah opens with a question to the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Have We not caused thy bosom to dilate?" The chest, made wide.
Then, a few lines later, the same sentence twice in a row: "But lo! with hardship goeth ease, Lo! with hardship goeth ease." Not after hardship. With it.
Ease arrives inside the hard thing, not only at the end of it. Something to tell a friend tonight: the Qur'an says that line twice, back to back, as if once wasn't enough for someone who's tired.
So the widening isn't a reward for surviving the tightening.
It comes from the same Giver, sometimes in the middle of the squeeze: a friend who shows up, a breath that goes all the way down, a wall that suddenly has eleven people painting it.

how: Muslims recite surah al-Sharh, the short surah of the widened chest, and its line 'with hardship goeth ease' is recited for comfort in hard times.

o: the One who opens and widens what was tight
the One who spreads His word to every land
the One who stretches time so work gets done

s: the Qur'an says ease comes only after the hardship is completely over
with hardship goeth ease: with, not only after. and it says it twice.
al-Basit and al-Qabid stand side by side in the traditional list
the hand that closes is the same hand that opens.

games.q: a friend just got through a brutal month and says, 'i guess the good part only starts once the bad part ends.' what does today's surah say?
o: with hardship goeth ease: the widening can come inside the hard part.
she's right: ease is the prize for finishing the hardship first.
hardship and ease have nothing to do with each other at all.
games.why: the surah says 'with', twice in a row. the widening isn't only a prize at the end; it can arrive in the middle.

practice: Sit up and let your shoulders fall away from your ears. Breathe in slowly and feel your ribs widen out to the sides, as if your chest were making room; breathe out and let it settle without collapsing.

Rest your hands on your knees and, over the next few breaths, let them turn palms up and open, the opposite of yesterday's fist. Feel the air on the open palms, and stay with that width for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Al-Basit: the Expander, who opens and widens, the chest, the heart, the means of life. The other half of al-Qabid.

orig.note: Arabic: the Expander, who opens and widens. beside al-Qabid in the traditional list.

carryVoice: Pocket this: the widening comes with the hardship, not only after it. See you tomorrow.
